correctness.rationale: The proof verifies the semisimple density identity, excludes matrix blocks, degree-one field factors and all field-profile dimension possibilities except (2,3) with radical dimension 2, then uses Peirce bimodule divisibility and a square-zero twisted action to classify the unique noncommutative equality ring. The cited Artin-Wedderburn and Wedderburn-Malcev theorems apply to finite-dimensional associative algebras over the perfect base field Fp. Exact arithmetic and representative multiplication were independently computed for p=2,3,5, including full associativity for p=2; finite checks are corroborating only.

value.rationale: The number and proportion of units are intrinsic algebraic invariants. The p^7 case is the first odd dimension where a noncommutative unital Fp algebra can exceed the local density 1-1/p; the theorem provides a sharp p-parametric upper bound, an explicit algebraic construction and a unique extremizer. The constraint forcing mixed finite-field residue degrees (2,3) and radical dimension two is structural, not a tabulated arbitrary example; the result does not claim a general dimension formula.
